name: Microsoft Teams
summary: Microsoft's hub for chat, channels and meetings, bundled with most Microsoft 365 plans. This entry covers chat and channels; for meetings, see the Zoom entry.

factors: Getting chat history out is slow, partial and administrator-only
Every team is backed by a Microsoft 365 group and a SharePoint site
Meetings, calendars and telephony all route through it
Partners and customers expect Teams meeting links
Bundled pricing makes it feel free

export.summary: There is no export button for users. Administrators of smaller tenants can request Microsoft's Teams data export tool, which takes weeks to be granted; larger tenants are left with compliance tooling or the Graph API.

methods.name: Teams data export tool
methods.detail: Requested through the Teams admin center, for tenants of up to about 500 users. Access can take around a month to arrive, and your tenant must stay active while you use it. It exports teams, channels and channel messages.

methods.name: Microsoft Graph export APIs
methods.detail: Programmatic access to all messages. Metered, requires an app registration with admin consent, and you write the converter yourself.

methods.name: Channel files
methods.detail: Files shared in channels live in the team's SharePoint site and can be copied out like any other SharePoint library.

caveats: Start the export request weeks before you plan to switch
Direct messages and private channels are the hardest to get out; plan to keep an archive for reference instead of migrating them
Do not cancel licences until the export has finished and been verified
Meeting recordings are stored in OneDrive and SharePoint, not in Teams itself

paths.verdict: The only option here with an official Teams importer, and a good fit if your team wants calmer, more organised conversations.

import.summary: Zulip's importer takes the output of Microsoft's Teams data export tool and recreates users, teams as channels and public channel history. Direct messages and private channels are not imported.

links.label: Zulip: migrating from other chat tools

transfers: Teams, as channels with their members
lost: Built-in meetings (Zulip hands calls to Jitsi or BigBlueButton)
Tabs, apps and Power Automate flows
Presence and calendar integration with Outlook

paths.verdict: The most familiar layout for people coming from Teams channels, if you accept starting with a clean history.

import.summary: There is no Teams importer. Recreate teams and channels, move files across from SharePoint, and start history fresh. Anyone determined to bring history must convert a Teams export into Mattermost's bulk-import format with their own scripts.

transfers: Team and channel structure, recreated by hand
lost: All message history, unless you write a converter
Group calls and meetings in the free edition
Tabs, apps and Power Automate flows
Presence and calendar integration with Outlook

paths.verdict: For organisations that need end-to-end encryption or want to federate with partners who also run Matrix.

import.summary: There is no importer. Recreate spaces and rooms and start history fresh. A Matrix bridge to Teams can relay messages both ways during the transition, but it needs its own setup and Microsoft app registration.

transfers: Team and channel structure, recreated as spaces and rooms
lost: Tabs, apps and Power Automate flows
Presence and calendar integration with Outlook
The simplicity of not thinking about encryption keys
